newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says cabinet talks with Chirac went well.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says cabinet talks with Chirac went well.

text.p: French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin presented his proposed cabinet list for key posts to President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday and said after their hour-long meeting that the talks had gone well.
Asked whether Chirac had agreed on the broad-left cabinet list, including two Communists, Jospin would only say: "I had a conversation with the president. This conversation went very well."

The president has to approve the appointment of ministers and the new government is traditionally announced by the secretary-general of the president's office on the steps of the Elysee presidential palace.
There was no immediate announcement after Jospin left Chirac's office.
Socialist party sources said Jospin discussed with Chirac the most "sensitive ministries", including foreign affairs and defence, interior and justice.
Close Jospin associate Dominique Strauss-Kahn, author of the Socialists' economic programme, was expected to be named finance minister, they said.
